title: Meta Launches Muse Ember, Its Smallest AI Model, on the Day Anthropic Unveiled Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
summary: Meta launches Muse Ember, its smallest and cheapest AI agent model at $0.10 per million tokens
detailed: Meta released Muse Ember, a small multimodal AI model priced at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens.
Muse Ember reads up to one million tokens at once and is designed for repetitive agent tasks like tool calling and document data extraction.
Meta claims Ember beats Claude Haiku 5.5 and OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna on intelligence per dollar across reasoning levels.
Independent benchmarks show Ember scoring lower on real coding tasks compared to Claude Haiku, highlighting trade-offs for developers.
sentences: Meta released Muse Ember on Monday, a small model sold on price, and it pulled the spotlight away from Anthropic's much-awaited Fable 5.2 on the very day the Claude models launched.
The model with the higher score is not the one getting the conversation.
Meta Superintelligence Labs put out Muse Ember on 9 November, the fourth model in its Muse family after Spark in April, the open-source Glimmer in August and the frontier Wonder in October.
It costs $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens, takes text, images, audio and video, and reads up to a million tokens at once.
Meta says it is available now through the Meta Model API and its Muse Code tool.
Ember is not meant to be the smartest model in the room.
Meta describes it as the one that does the repetitive part of agent work: calling tools in order, routing requests, pulling data out of documents, making small code fixes.
Its own line sums up the plan.
Wonder plans, and Ember handles the volume.
The pitch is intelligence per dollar.
Meta says Ember beats Claude Haiku 5.5 and OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna on that measure at every reasoning level.
Independent numbers from Artificial Analysis put its Intelligence Index score at 36, almost level with the much larger Muse Spark 1.3 at 37, while a task costs about $0.14 against $2.39.
If that holds up, it is a serious number for anyone paying for agents that run thousands of times a day.
Read the caveats before the headline.
On FrontierCode 2.0, a test of real coding tasks, Claude Haiku scored 34.9 percent and Ember 27.2 percent.
So on the work developers care about most, the cheaper model from Meta is behind.
Most of the other benchmark wins come from Meta's own tests, and the comparison with open-source flash models only says Ember is cost-competitive, not better.
Treat "more intelligence per dollar" as a claim to test on your own workload.

S&P's report flagged Meta's lack of a cloud business to resell AI compute through, unlike Microsoft or Google, and projected a $71 billion free cash flow deficit in 2027 alone. - how to interpret Meta's negative credit outlook - Meta's AI spending outrunning free cash flow
Anthropic announced Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, two flagship models for demanding technical work.
Fable is open to paying users and has safeguards that block risky cybersecurity and biology tasks.
Mythos removes some of those limits and is restricted to organisations approved through its cybersecurity and life sciences verification programmes.
Pricing falls to $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output, down from $10 and $50, and output is up to 30 percent faster.
On the Artificial Analysis index Fable 5.2 scores 65, ahead of every rival listed, though it trails on some agentic and terminal-coding tests and costs far more per task than Opus 5.5.
Anthropic itself still tells most people to start with Opus 5.5.
The launch also lands ahead of the company's expected IPO.
Anthropic had the stronger model and Meta had the louder story.
Fable 5.2 was the launch people had been waiting for, yet the talk on launch day turned to a $0.10 model from Meta.
The reason is simple: the two companies are playing different games.
Anthropic is pushing the ceiling for hard problems and trimming the price a little.
Meta is pushing the floor, making the boring repeated work cheap enough to run all day.
For a team building agents, the second game often matters more to the bill.
The models that finish a hard task once are rarely the ones that run a million times a month.
If Ember's price holds and its quality is good enough for routing and extraction, it puts pressure on every small model from the other labs.
That is a quieter story than a frontier launch, and in our view a bigger one for most businesses.
Attention is not quality, and Meta still has to prove Ember on real workloads.
Test it on your own tasks before you switch anything, and do not take a launch-day chart as proof.
